newsitem.title: USA: Stock prices rattled by leap in trade deficit.
newsitem.headline: Stock prices rattled by leap in trade deficit.

text.p: Stock prices were mostly lower Wednesday after a report that surging U.S. imports sparked a leap of nearly 43 percent leap in the nation's trade deficit cast doubt about third-quarter economic growth.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 15.17 points at 5,873.66. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 12-8 on moderate volume of 217 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The Commerce Department said the trade gap ballooned by 42.6 percent in July to $11.68 billion from $8.19 billion in June. The magnitude of the deficit shocked economists, who had generally forecast a gap of $8.8 billion.

Analysts said the trade deficit, which is the largest since late 1987, threw into question just how robust a rate of growth the economy continues to enjoy and further clouded the near-term outlook for interest rates.

"If you're an economist, you worry a lot about this number because it says gross domestic product may be weaker than economists are forecasting for the third quarter," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
"Net exports are one of the crucial components of GDP and this says net exports are a big minus," he said.
The data came a day after the Dow index paused in its run at the psychologically important 6,000-point level after it set record high closes on Monday and Friday.
"Once you get to these threshold numbers, there's always temporary resistance," said Tom Carpenter, managing director and chief economist at ASB Capital Management Inc.
The market was likely to be erratic through Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, which will decide whether to raise interest rates or keep them unchanged.
"If we can get past next week, and the Fed does not raise rates, that's when we could make the final lunge toward 6,000," Carpenter said.

While the trade gap report suggested economic growth may be slowing in the third quarter, analysts said one month of trade data was not sufficient to settle market nerves about the possibility that the Fed will boost short-term interest rates.

"If there has ever been a high level of uncertainty about what the decision will be, this is it," said Johnson. "Portfolio managers just try to come in to the decision fairly neutral, knowing you could get a big surprise."
Meanwhile, the shares of oil companies were higher amid increased tensions between Syria and Israel and a report of Iraqi shelling of a Kurdish refugee camp.

Syria said the policies of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had caused tension in the Middle East and could lead to war. The remarks, which appeared in Syria's official press, were the latest sign of tension between the two countries, fuelled by Syrian troop movements in Lebanon.
Texaco Inc. was up 1-1/2 to 95-1/8 and Exxon Corp. rose 3/4 to 85-7/8. Crude oil jumped 57 cents to $23.88 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Sun Microsystems Inc. rose 1-1/2 to 60 after the company announced a technology alliance with Apple Computer Corp., whose stock was up 3/4 to 23-3/4.
Netscape Communications Corp. fell 4-1/4 to 41-3/4 after Merrill Lynch downgraded the stock.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 0.67 at 1,203.98 and the American Stock Exchange index lost 0.66 at 566.50.
